newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS upgrades CNR with stable trend.
newsitem.headline: DBRS upgrades CNR with stable trend.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Friday that it upgraded the senior unsecured debt rating of Canadian National Railway Co to BBB (high) with a stable trend.
DBRS also said it assigned a commercial paper rating of R-1 (Low) to CNR with a stable trend.

The debt rating agency said the upgrade recognizes the steady improvement in operations through 1996, following the privatization of the railway in November 1995. Cost containment through workforce reductions, improved asset utilization and network rationalization were primarily responsible for the increase in earnings, DBRS said.

The company's balance sheet continued to improve in 1996, after debt reductions associated with the 1995 privatization, DBRS said. Strong operating cash flow helped offset high capital expenditures and cash payments for employee separations, the agency said.
Operating cash flow should maintain a stable balance sheet into 2000, with the potential for further debt reduction if the current business cycle remains positive, DBRS.
